benefits: A MAECI scholarship aims to help cover the costs of living and studying in Italy, and is paid only for the periods the grantee actually spends in Italy

A nine-month scholarship starts on 1 November of the year of publication of the Call and ends on 31 July of the following year; a three-month scholarship can be benefited in a period of study starting on 1 January and ending by 30 September of the year of publication of the Call
Renewal: the awarding of a new MAECI Scholarship to beneficiaries of the previous Call who submit a regular application to continue their study programme, in accordance with Article 3 of the Call
eligibility: Applications are accepted from citizens of the countries included in the eligible countries list published in the Call; if your country is not on the list you cannot apply
You can indicate a maximum of three course options, even in different institutions or universities, but all three must be of the same type
It is not possible to apply for online study programmes, as the scholarship only covers onsite attendance of academic courses on Italian territory
Applying for a MAECI grant and enrolling at the university or institution are two separate and different procedures
requirements: Applications are accepted exclusively through the Study in Italy website after completing the sign-up procedure; applications and documents submitted through any other means of transmission are not accepted
Documents must be uploaded exclusively in PDF format, one file per field (multiple documents may be merged into a single file), each file not exceeding 2 MB
It is not necessary to upload translated or legalized documents; a scan of the original documents in PDF format is required

Supplementary documents as per Article 7.2 (including language certificates) must be uploaded strictly by 14:00 Italian time on 1 July 2026, otherwise the application cannot be evaluated; supplementary documents cannot be submitted for intensive Italian language and culture courses or renewals
documents: Curriculum Vitae; the academic qualification valid for admission to the chosen programme (with achieved or expected marks); the transcript of records

Language certificate from an official certification body or other documentation certifying proficiency with specific reference to CEFR levels; Duolingo certificates are accepted exclusively for the English language
Motivation letter describing your personal story, education background, academic interests and the purpose and goals of your study project, on plain paper and not exceeding 500 words
Other documents: any useful element that can be positively evaluated; an admission letter for the chosen programme or a letter of recommendation may be uploaded
For PhD applications: the admission letter is required (a supervisor invitation letter may be uploaded until the admission letter is issued; pre-admission letters are not considered valid)
selection_criteria: At the end of the evaluation, the relevant Italian Diplomatic representation publishes the ranking of winners and any reserves on its website; the merit ranking is unquestionable and only winners are notified via the Study in Italy portal
coverage: A MAECI scholarship aims to help cover the costs of living and studying in Italy, paid only for the periods the grantee actually spends in Italy (nine-month grants: 1 November - 31 July)
application_method: Sign up and submit the application exclusively through the Study in Italy website during the Call window

Select the type of study programme (Master's Degree, Higher Education for Fine Arts Music and Dance, PhD, research project, intensive Italian language and culture course, or Bachelor's/single-cycle renewal for previous 'Costruiamo il futuro' beneficiaries)
Indicate up to three course options of the same type, then upload all required documents in PDF before the deadline
official.application_route: Apply online exclusively through the official Study in Italy platform (studyinitaly.esteri.it) when the annual Call opens; rankings are published by the Italian Diplomatic representation.
official.study_mode: Onsite attendance on Italian territory; online study programmes are not eligible
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of the countries on the eligible countries list published in the Call
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the grants are for foreign citizens to study in Italy, published as the Italian Government scholarships for foreign students
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's Degree, Higher Education in Fine Arts Music and Dance (AFAM), PhD, research project, or intensive Italian language and culture course; Bachelor's degree/single-cycle Master's degree exclusively for students who have already benefited from the 'Costruiamo il futuro' scholarship under Articles 1.6 and 3 of the Call
official.research_requirement: Research projects are one of the offered study types; the title of the research project is entered in the course selection
official.duration: Nine months (1 November - 31 July) for most study programmes; three months for the intensive Italian language and culture course
official.description: Italian Government (MAECI) Study Grants are scholarships for foreign citizens to study in Italy at Master's, AFAM, PhD or research level or to attend intensive Italian language and culture courses, applied for exclusively through the official Study in Italy platform.
official.program_type: Government grant for international students (Italian Government / MAECI scholarship)
official.english_requirement: A certificate issued by an official certification body or other documents certifying language proficiency with specific reference to CEFR levels; Duolingo certificates are accepted exclusively for the English language. Italian or English requirements follow the Call, and the certificate can be uploaded as a supplementary document by 14:00 Italian time on 1 July 2026 if listed in the merit ranking (not possible for language courses and renewals).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly grant for living and studying costs, not a full scholarship: it is paid only for the months actually in Italy, and nine-month grants run 1 November to 31 July, so plan your own funds around the rest of the year. Applications are free and go only through the official Study in Italy platform - never pay an agent - and you may list up to three course options of the same type. The A.Y. 2026-2027 round has already closed with the final ranking published on 3 June 2026, and the portal had not yet announced the next call as of 10 October 2026, so use the interval to line up your CEFR-language certificate and supervisor contacts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-motivated graduates and PhD applicants who can top up the Italian living grant with their own funds and apply separately for university admission.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on the eligible countries list in the Call - if it is not, you cannot apply at all
Choose up to three course options, all of the same type, at institutions listed on the Universitaly portal
Start the separate university enrolment process early: the grant application does not enrol you

Prepare your language certificate from an official body with an explicit CEFR level (Duolingo only works for English), and be ready to supplement it by 14:00 Italian time on 1 July if you make the ranking
Keep the motivation letter under 500 words and upload everything as PDF files under 2 MB
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 July 14:00 Italian time supplementary-documents deadline, after which the application cannot be evaluated
Proposing an online study programme, which is expressly ineligible
Uploading translated or legalized paperwork that was never required, wasting time and stalling the real gaps (qualification, transcript, language certificate)
Assuming the MAECI grant also secures university admission - it does not
Mixing course types across the three options, which the platform disallows
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the monthly grant: accommodation outside the 1 November - 31 July window, travel to Italy, enrolment taxes or tuition the institution charges, and general living costs.
document_audit: PhD applicants must upload the admission letter; until it exists, the supervisor's invitation letter substitutes, but pre-admission letters are never accepted
Renewal applicants need a certificate or hand-signed self-declaration of university credits (CFU) obtained with marks
No translations or legalizations are needed - original scans in PDF only, merged where necessary, each file under 2 MB
Supplementary documents - including language certificates - cannot be submitted for intensive language courses or renewals, so those must be complete at submission
alerts: The next Call is not yet published; the grant amount itself is fixed only in each Call, which is why no figure appears here
Only applications submitted through the Study in Italy website are accepted - other channels are not
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Wait for the Call on studyinitaly.esteri.it, apply free of charge on the platform with up to three same-type course options, upload the PDF document set before the deadline, supplement by 1 July 14:00 Italian time if ranked, then await the ranking published by the Italian Diplomatic representation.
